experiment: phi calibration, steady state, real model
method: the repo's own LINGBOT_DUMP_QKV hook saved a real steady-state q/k/v (fires at k.shape[1] >= 27000) during `lingbot clip --frame_num 193 --bench` (16.3 FPS); row maxima computed offline from it in fp32, tiled over keys
verdict: C5 with a single global phi is DEAD, and so is per-layer phi: the spread is 29.6 log2 BETWEEN HEADS OF ONE LAYER, 8x the fp8 window. A phi set for the hottest head flushes the coldest heads' P to zero. C5 would need a per-(layer,head) phi tensor plus offline calibration and a saturation guard - far more than the 'one constant' the 8.7 % was measured with.
caveat: one layer, one forward, one scene. The per-head pattern may differ by layer and may drift across scenes/rollouts, which would make calibration harder still, not easier.
instrumentation_note: the phi_calib.py hook never fired because the DiT is torch.compiled and the compiled graph binds the original attention() object, so patching module references afterwards has no effect; the repo's own in-function dump hook works because it lives inside that original function. Any future in-model instrumentation must either live inside attention() itself or run with compilation genuinely off.

red_team.verdict_challenged: a reviewer called the 29.6 log2 spread implausible and suspected a permute/stride bug
red_team.validation_run: pod 20, 2026-09-22: permute checked (q[0].permute(1,0,2) -> [12,6032,128] = [H,L,D], correct); per-head max raw logits checked against their Cauchy-Schwarz bounds
red_team.outcome: objection REFUTED. The layout is correct and every logit is inside its norm bound; the spread is caused by a ~7x range in per-head key norms (mean |k| 2.8 to 19.1), which RMSNorm's learned per-channel scale permits. The units convention is also correct: S*sm_scale*log2(e) converts the natural-log exponent to base 2, which is what the kernel uses.
red_team.remaining_caveat: still one layer, one forward, one scene; the per-head pattern may vary by layer and drift across scenes, which would make calibration harder, not easier
